description: NULL placement in ORDER BY. Snowflake's DEFAULT is NULLS LAST for ASC and NULLS FIRST for DESC - the OPPOSITE convention of several other engines - and an explicit NULLS FIRST / NULLS LAST overrides either default. The same defaults govern a WINDOW's ORDER BY, so under ROW_NUMBER() the NULL row ranks last ascending and first descending, which is asserted here from both directions in one query. Converted 1:1 from query/OrderByNullsPlacementTest (now retired); the Java's assertOrder helper walked the rows by index, so the converted steps pin the whole ordered row set. The same defaults are also asserted from the three-valued-logic side in query-null-three-valued-logic.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, n INTEGER)
SELECT n FROM t ORDER BY n
SELECT n FROM t ORDER BY n ASC
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, n INTEGER)
SELECT n FROM t ORDER BY n DESC
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, n INTEGER)
SELECT n FROM t ORDER BY n ASC NULLS FIRST
SELECT n FROM t ORDER BY n DESC NULLS LAST
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, n INTEGER)
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n) AS asc_rn, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY n DESC) AS desc_rn FROM t ORDER BY id
